Electronic circuit · Physical prototype

Automatic Night Lamp Using NAND Gate

An ambient-light-responsive lamp circuit using an LDR sensing arrangement and NAND-gate logic to switch an LED according to surrounding light conditions.

LDR / GL55377400 NAND ICVoltage dividerBreadboard
View technical case study

Problem & objective

Provide automatic light switching based on ambient illumination without relying on a microcontroller. The circuit responds to changes in light detected by an LDR.

Design approach

  • Use an LDR in a resistive sensing network to make the circuit respond to light intensity.
  • Use a voltage-divider arrangement to create a changing input voltage as illumination changes.
  • Apply NAND-gate logic to control the output stage and LED.
  • Assemble the circuit on a breadboard and observe its response under different lighting conditions.

Implementation evidence

The report identifies this as a group mini-project. The portfolio describes the circuit and prototype evidence without assigning unverified individual task ownership.

Skills demonstrated

Logic-gate fundamentals, LDR interfacing, voltage-divider analysis, circuit interpretation, breadboard assembly and basic functional testing.

Additional result: Iterative convergence

The mismatch reduces across iterations, illustrating the convergence behaviour of the numerical solution.

Power-system analysis · Numerical computation

Load Flow Analysis of a 3-Bus Power System Using Newton–Raphson Method

A numerical study of a three-bus network to determine bus voltages, power flow and transmission losses, with convergence and voltage-profile plots generated in GNU Octave.

GNU OctaveY-BusNewton–RaphsonPower flow
View technical case study

Problem & objective

Analyse the steady-state operating condition of a three-bus power system and obtain the bus voltage magnitudes and angles, power-flow quantities and system losses.

Method and workflow

  • Define the bus and transmission-line data for the network.
  • Form the bus-admittance (Y-Bus) matrix.
  • Set the slack-bus reference and initialise unknown bus voltages.
  • Calculate real and reactive power mismatches.
  • Apply iterative voltage updates and monitor mismatch reduction.
  • Calculate line power flows and total transmission losses.
  • Plot the voltage profile and iteration convergence in GNU Octave.

Reported numerical results

  • Slack-bus voltage: 1.0500 pu.
  • Bus 2 voltage: 0.9504 pu.
  • Bus 3 voltage: 0.9435 pu.
  • Reported total transmission loss: approximately 0.02623 pu.

Skills demonstrated

Power-system modelling, Y-Bus matrix formation, iterative numerical methods, GNU Octave scripting, result interpretation and engineering plotting.

This project is presented as your individual work, as you clarified. The report contains group-member names, but this portfolio follows your clarification about your own completion of the project.

Power electronics · Converter design

300 W DC–AC Inverter Using SG3525 PWM Controller

A power-electronics design study of a DC–AC inverter using an SG3525 PWM controller, MOSFET switching stage and centre-tapped transformer arrangement.

SG3525PWM controlIRF3205 MOSFETPush-pull
View technical case study

Design objective

Study a 300 W inverter arrangement intended to convert a low-voltage DC supply into an AC output using controlled switching and transformer action.

Functional stages

  • SG3525 oscillator and PWM control generate alternating drive signals.
  • Power MOSFETs form the push-pull switching stage.
  • A centre-tapped transformer couples the switching stage to the higher-voltage output side.
  • Timing and control components set oscillator behaviour and support soft-start/dead-time functions described in the report.

Key components discussed

SG3525 PWM controller, IRF3205 MOSFETs, centre-tapped transformer, timing resistors and capacitors, diodes, heat sinks and DC source.

Skills demonstrated

Power-electronic converter concepts, PWM control, MOSFET switching, transformer operation, circuit reading and component-function analysis.

Presented as a design/report project. The website does not claim a physically assembled or load-tested 300 W inverter because supporting test evidence has not been provided.

IoT · Embedded software · Cloud dashboard

Cloud-Integrated IoT System for Real-Time Soil Moisture Monitoring

An IoT workflow for acquiring soil-moisture readings, transferring them through a serial data gateway, storing them in the cloud and presenting them through a web dashboard.

ArduinoPython / PySerialFirebaseHTML · CSS · JS
View technical case study

Problem & objective

Make soil-moisture readings accessible beyond the microcontroller by connecting sensor acquisition to cloud storage and a browser-based visualisation interface.

System data flow

  • A capacitive soil-moisture sensor provides an analogue signal.
  • The microcontroller reads and reports the sensor value over USB serial.
  • A Python process uses PySerial to receive serial data and handle cloud communication.
  • Firebase Firestore stores readings and timestamps.
  • A web dashboard presents the current reading and historical trend.

Dashboard features documented

Moisture gauge, current moisture value, historical graph, connection status and last-updated information.

Skills demonstrated

Microcontroller programming, analogue sensor acquisition, serial communication, Python scripting, cloud database integration and web-based data visualisation.

The report describes Arduino Uno, while the supplied Wokwi evidence screenshot shows an Arduino Nano simulation. The portfolio keeps this distinction visible rather than treating the screenshot as proof of a physical Nano build.

Final-year project · IoT · Environmental monitoring

AquaPulse – Water Quality Monitoring and Mapping

A multi-parameter water-quality monitoring concept combining sensor inputs, ESP32 processing, local display and a proposed location-based web mapping platform.

ESP32Sensor integrationWokwiTFT / SPIWeb mapping
View technical case study

Problem & objective

Present water-quality information in a location-oriented format so that readings from monitoring points can be understood through colour-coded station indicators and parameter details.

Prototype and processing

  • Use ESP32 as the embedded controller.
  • Read and process water-quality parameter inputs, including pH, turbidity, TDS, dissolved oxygen, chlorine, ammonia, nitrate and temperature.
  • Use an ILI9341 TFT display over SPI for local information display.
  • Compare values with configured thresholds and show status indicators.
  • Develop a web interface concept for station information and geographical presentation.

Simulation evidence

The supplied Wokwi screenshot shows the ESP32, simulated parameter inputs, temperature sensor, TFT display and status indicators. ORP and conductivity are marked as simulated in the screenshot.

Skills demonstrated

Embedded C/C++, ESP32 pin configuration, sensor interfacing concepts, SPI display integration, threshold-based classification, simulation and system architecture.

The Wokwi evidence is a simulation. The report identifies physical sensor integration, calibration and real-world validation as further development work. The project is presented as a team project; individual task ownership is not assigned here.

PCB design · Electronic hardware

ESP32-S3 Sensor Interface PCB

A PCB design exercise integrating an ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N4 module with MPU6050 and BMP280 sensor interfaces, supported by a schematic and routed board layout in EasyEDA.

EasyEDA StandardESP32-S3MPU6050BMP280I²C
View technical case study

Design requirement

Create a board-level design that connects an ESP32-S3 module to two sensor devices, with power, ground and I²C communication connections.

Design workflow

  • Select the microcontroller module and sensor footprints/symbols.
  • Prepare the schematic and connect the power rails, ground and I²C signal lines.
  • Transfer the schematic into PCB layout.
  • Arrange components and route the board connections.
  • Review the board in 2D and 3D views.

Evidence

The supplied screenshots show the schematic, PCB photo view and 3D board view in EasyEDA Standard.

Skills demonstrated

Schematic capture, component selection, footprint awareness, I²C wiring, PCB placement, track routing and 3D design review.

This is presented as a PCB design deliverable. No claim of fabrication, assembly or electrical testing is made without corresponding evidence.

Building electrical design · QElectroTech

Electrical Design of a Two-Storey Commercial Building

A complete electrical documentation exercise for a two-storey commercial building with a reported connected load of 45 kW and a 415 V, 50 Hz, three-phase, four-wire supply.

QElectroTech45 kW connected load415 V, 3-phaseBOQ
View technical case study

Design workflow

  • Study lighting, power, air-conditioning and equipment requirements.
  • Prepare the SLD and determine the main distribution arrangement.
  • Develop the MDB, outgoing feeder, load and cable schedules.
  • Prepare lighting and power layouts for both floors.
  • Develop wiring, cable-routing and conduit-routing drawings.
  • Document earthing and lightning-protection arrangements.
  • Include load, cable-sizing, voltage-drop and short-circuit calculations as reported in the project.
  • Prepare BOQ, material schedule and general electrical specifications.

Skills demonstrated

QElectroTech drafting, electrical distribution planning, load scheduling, cable documentation, protective-device coordination concepts, earthing layouts and engineering report preparation.

This is a design and documentation project, not a claim of site installation or commissioning.
